Balanced V-fold cross-validation

Source: R/balanced_vfold_cv.R
balanced_vfold_cv.Rd

balanced_vfold_cv() splits the data into v folds of about equal size that are similar on several variables at once. Each fold is used once as the assessment set, and the other folds form the analysis set.

Usage

balanced_vfold_cv(
  data,
  v = 10,
  repeats = 1,
  balance = NULL,
  exact = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  method = "anticlust",
  options = list(),
  na = "error",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

v

The number of folds.

repeats

The number of times to repeat the V-fold partitioning.

balance

<tidy-select> Columns to balance across the sets. Numeric columns are standardized. So are Date, POSIXct, and difftime columns, as numbers of days or seconds. Factor, character, and logical columns become one indicator column per level.

exact

<tidy-select> Categorical columns to stratify exactly. Each combination of levels is one stratum. In each stratum, the count in every set is the floor or the ceiling of its proportional share, based on the actual size of that set. For folds, the counts of a stratum also differ by at most one over the folds whenever both rules can hold at once. With group, these counts are numbers of groups, not rows. exact does the job of strata in rsample, but it takes several columns and its counts are exact. Numeric columns with whole-number values are treated as categories. Put continuous columns in balance, or use cut() to make a factor if you need exact counts within ranges. A stratum whose share of the smallest set is under one row (or group) can be missing from some sets. If more than half of the strata are missing from at least one set, you get a warning.

group

<tidy-select> One column with group IDs. All rows of a group go to the same set. See Details.

method

The balancing method: "anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", or "interaction". See Details.

options

A named list of options for the method. See Details.

na

What to do with missing values in the balance and exact columns. "error" (the default) stops with an error. "include" balances on which values are missing; see Missing values. The group column must not have missing values either way.

...

Not used. Must be empty.

Value

A tibble with class balanced_vfold_cv and rset. It has a splits column of rsplit objects and one or two ID columns.

Methods

  • "anticlust" (default) uses k-plus anticlustering (Papenberg, 2024) with anticlust::fast_anticlustering(). It makes the means and the variances of the sets similar. Options are:

    • moments (default 2): the highest moment to balance. 1 balances means only, 3 adds skewness, and 4 adds kurtosis.

    • covariances (default FALSE): also balance the product of each pair of balance columns.

    • k_neighbours (default Inf): the number of nearest neighbours each row may swap with. Inf tries every swap, so the run time grows quickly with the number of rows. A small number, such as 20, is much faster on large data, but categorical balance columns can end up less balanced. Check the result with balance_check().

    • local_maximum (default TRUE): repeat the exchange passes until a pass makes no swap (at most 100 passes). FALSE runs one pass.

    • repetitions (default 1): the number of random starts. The best result is kept.

  • "twinning" uses twinning::multiplet() for folds, or twinning::twin() for v = 2 with strategy 1 or 2, which then give the same result. Options are strategy (1, 2, or 3; strategy 2 needs v to be a power of 2) and leaf_size. Strata with fewer than 2 * v rows (or groups) are assigned at random. The twinning package is required.

  • "rerandomize" draws stratified random splits and keeps the first one whose Mahalanobis imbalance is under a threshold (Morgan and Rubin, 2012). For folds, the imbalance is the largest over the "one fold versus the rest" comparisons. The threshold is the p_accept quantile of the imbalance over pilot draws made with the same exact and group constraints (max(100, min(ceiling(10 / p_accept), max_draws)) draws). Draws that tie with the threshold are accepted at random, so that the acceptance rate is close to p_accept even for discrete data. If p_accept is below 1 / max(100, max_draws), the pilot draws can't resolve it, and the threshold is the best pilot draw. Options are p_accept, the target acceptance rate (default 0.1), and max_draws (default 1000). If no draw meets the threshold, the best draw is used with a warning.

  • "interaction" cuts numeric columns into quantile bins, crosses all bins, and stratifies at random. It is a baseline that shows how crossed strata become sparse. Options are n_bins (default 4) and pool (default 0.1): cells with less than this fraction of the rows are pooled.

The method balances the columns left after standardizing: constant columns are dropped, and with group, so are columns whose group means are all equal up to rounding error (see Groups). If none are left, for example with only exact columns and no group, the method doesn't run and the sets are drawn at random, within the exact strata if there are any. The limits the method itself checks, such as twinning's strategy 2 needing a power of 2, then don't apply. The options are still checked, and the split functions still check that twinning can make prop.

Groups

If you use group, each group becomes one row before the method runs. This row holds the group means of the standardized balance columns and the log of the group size. The group size is added only if a balance column is left after standardizing or there are exact columns, and it is dropped if all groups have the same size. The method assigns groups, and then each row gets the set of its group. The number of groups per set follows the target proportions, so the number of rows per set is only approximate. exact columns must be constant within each group.

Missing values

With na = "include", rows with missing values stay in the split, and the method also balances how often each column is missing. The data in the split keep their missing values, so your model can handle them its own way, for example with a recipe.

  • In a numeric, logical, Date, POSIXct, or difftime column in balance, missing values get the mean of the observed values, and an indicator column of which values are missing is balanced too. With the share missing balanced, balancing the filled column also balances the mean of the observed values. The filled values all sit at the mean, so the spread of the observed values is balanced less closely.

  • In a factor or character column in balance, a missing value is one more level.

  • In exact, a missing value is one more level, so the rows with a missing value in a column are spread over the sets by exact counts like any other stratum. With group, a missing value counts as a level when exact columns are checked for being constant within each group, so a group with some rows at site "A" and some with a missing site is an error.

Each indicator column is standardized like the other columns. When few values are missing, the rows with a missing value are far from the rest on that column (about 10 standard deviations at 1% missing), as rows of a rare level are. A column with no observed values is an error.

Rows with a missing group ID could belong to one unit or to several, so group must not have missing values. Give those rows their own IDs, or one shared ID, depending on which is true.

Use with tune

tune and rsample::reshuffle_rset() find the function that made an rset by its class name. They only find balanced_vfold_cv() when balancedsample is attached with library(balancedsample). If you call balancedsample::balanced_vfold_cv() without attaching the package, tune::fit_resamples() and tune::tune_grid() fail with "Could not find function".

If a workflow has a postprocessor that must be trained, such as a calibration from the tailor package, tune splits each analysis set again. That inner split is a balanced_initial_split() with the same balance, exact, group, na, method, and options (without twinning's strategy), and with prop = 1 - 1/v. With na = "include", a column with no observed values in the analysis set is left out of the inner split.

References

Morgan, K. L., & Rubin, D. B. (2012). Rerandomization to improve covariate balance in experiments. The Annals of Statistics, 40(2), 1263-1282. doi:10.1214/12-AOS1008

Papenberg, M. (2024). K-plus anticlustering: An improved k-means criterion for maximizing between-group similarity. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 77(1), 80-102. doi:10.1111/bmsp.12315

Papenberg, M., & Klau, G. W. (2021). Using anticlustering to partition data sets into equivalent parts. Psychological Methods, 26(2), 161-174. doi:10.1037/met0000301

Vakayil, A., & Joseph, V. R. (2022). Data twinning. Statistical Analysis and Data Mining, 15(5), 598-610. doi:10.1002/sam.11574

See also

balanced_initial_split(), balance_check()

Examples

set.seed(1)
folds <- balanced_vfold_cv(
  sim_patients,
  v = 5,
  balance = c(age, income),
  exact = c(diagnosis, site)
)
folds
#> # 5-fold balanced cross-validation (anticlust), balancing age, income,
#> # stratified by diagnosis, site
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   splits           id   
#>   <list>           <chr>
#> 1 <split [240/60]> Fold1
#> 2 <split [240/60]> Fold2
#> 3 <split [240/60]> Fold3
#> 4 <split [240/60]> Fold4
#> 5 <split [240/60]> Fold5
balance_check(folds)
#> # Balance check: 5 splits, 4 variables
#> # 0 of 5 splits have a variable with |SMD| > 0.1, mean energy distance 0.031
#> 
#> id     max |SMD|  variable         mean |SMD|  over 0.1  energy
#> Fold1     0.026   site: C             0.00967       0/4  0.0277
#> Fold2     0.026   site: A             0.00941       0/4  0.0361
#> Fold3     0.0373  diagnosis: mild     0.0187        0/4  0.0276
#> Fold4     0.026   site: C             0.00955       0/4  0.0309
#> Fold5     0.026   site: A             0.0091        0/4  0.0327
#> 
#> # summary() gives this table as a tibble, and tibble::as_tibble() gives all
#> # 45 rows.

# Other methods
balanced_vfold_cv(
  sim_patients,
  v = 5,
  balance = c(age, income),
  method = "rerandomize"
)
#> # 5-fold balanced cross-validation (rerandomize), balancing age, income
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   splits           id   
#>   <list>           <chr>
#> 1 <split [240/60]> Fold1
#> 2 <split [240/60]> Fold2
#> 3 <split [240/60]> Fold3
#> 4 <split [240/60]> Fold4
#> 5 <split [240/60]> Fold5
balanced_vfold_cv(
  sim_patients,
  v = 5,
  balance = c(age, income),
  method = "twinning"
)
#> # 5-fold balanced cross-validation (twinning), balancing age, income
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   splits           id   
#>   <list>           <chr>
#> 1 <split [240/60]> Fold1
#> 2 <split [240/60]> Fold2
#> 3 <split [240/60]> Fold3
#> 4 <split [240/60]> Fold4
#> 5 <split [240/60]> Fold5
